description:
A mutual contradiction between two beliefs whose evidence sets do not overlap at all.

Rules out a criterion that fires on conflict alone. This is the *ordinary* resolvable disagreement - two beliefs, each with its own observations, one of which is probably wrong - and it is what experiments 3 and 4 were entirely about. Underdetermination is the case where no evidence separates the rivals; here every record separates them, since each is held by exactly one side.

The counterpart to `shared_evidence_no_conflict`: between them they pin that both halves of the criterion carry weight. A criterion satisfying only the conflict half would derive here and be wrong in the most consequential direction, since it would relabel every ordinary dispute in the web as unresolvable.

expect.note: Structural. The conflict condition is satisfied and the evidence condition is not.

evidence.summary: A row count taken after the migration matches the pre-migration count.
Table checksums agree on both sides of the migration.
Three customer records present in the backup are absent from the migrated table.
The migration log records two constraint violations that were skipped.

beliefs.proposition: The migration preserved every row in the ledger table.
The migration dropped rows from the ledger table.
